g.text: ASK (PICO)
patient, action,
compare, outcome
FIND
PubMed, CINAHL,
HINARI, guidelines
JUDGE
hierarchy + CRAAP
+ relevance!
APPLY
patient + context
+ evaluate!
EBP in 4 moves: PICO question → systematic search → critical appraisal → applied +
evaluated with the patient. "We've always done it" is not evidence; neither is one blog.
PICO EXAMPLE: "In post-op adults (P), does chewing gum (I) vs nil-by-mouth (C) speed bowel
recovery (O)?" — searchable words fall straight out: gum, ileus, post-op, RCT.
HIERARCHY (top wins): systematic reviews + guidelines → RCTs → cohort → case-control →
case series → expert opinion. Ghana shortcut: national protocols + WHO guidelines FIRST
(context-fitted!), then HINARI free full-texts, then PubMed abstracts.
CRAAP TEST: Currency (2024 beats 1998!) · Relevance (Ghana wards?) · Authority (who wrote?
funded by whom?) · Accuracy (methods? numbers honest?) · Purpose (inform or sell?). Fails
any two? Find better. Predatory journals flatter: "publish in 3 days!" = pay, no review.
APPLY WITH JUDGMENT: evidence + patient values + YOUR expertise + setting reality (M01
wisdom!). RCT says drug X; patient can't afford it; guideline offers affordable Y — Y with
follow-up IS evidence-based care. Then EVALUATE: did it work? document + share.
SEARCH SKILLS (exam!): keywords + synonyms + AND/OR + filters (free full-text, 5 years,
humans) → scan abstracts → fetch 3 best → appraise → cite. Ten focused minutes beats an
hour of scrolling. Save searches; set alerts on your topic.
JOURNAL CLUB: one paper + one ward question + 30 minutes monthly = unit EBP culture. Present:
PICO, design, results in plain words, "should WE change?" — vote, pilot, measure (M05.2!).
LINKS: PRO-II M4/M5 QI + research · NUT guidelines · GER protocols.
MANTRA: "ask it, find it, judge it, use it — then check it worked."
